idh.reasoning: The patient's advanced age (74 years) is the single strongest predictor for IDH-wildtype status. The imaging features strongly corroborate this prediction. The tumor is a large, deeply infiltrative mass with extensive necrosis (39.38% of the core), which are hallmark features of glioblastoma, IDH-wildtype. Furthermore, the tumor exhibits a very sharp transition zone on FLAIR (median thickness 0.75 mm), which is characteristic of IDH-wildtype gliomas, in contrast to the ill-defined borders often seen in IDH-mutant tumors. Critically, the T2-FLAIR mismatch sign, a specific marker for IDH-mutant astrocytoma, is absent. The only mildly contradictory feature is the 'Mild' enhancement quality, but the presence of any enhancement and, more importantly, extensive necrosis, overwhelmingly supports an IDH-wildtype prediction.

The presence of extensive necrosis (Proportion Necrosis: 39.38%) and contrast enhancement are features strongly associated with astrocytic lineage tumors (non-codeleted) or glioblastoma, and are rare in oligodendrogliomas. The tumor's highly infiltrative nature, with deep white matter invasion, ependymal spread, and crossing of the midline, also points towards a more aggressive, non-codeleted phenotype. While the frontal lobe location is common for oligodendrogliomas, this is a non-specific feature and is outweighed by the strong evidence against co-deletion.

The metadata indicates a very high 'Proportion Necrosis' of 39.38%. This finding alone is the strongest indicator for a grade 4 tumor. This is further supported by the presence of contrast enhancement, a large tumor volume (231.95 mL), significant mass effect ('midline_shift_present': 'Yes'), and an aggressive infiltrative pattern ('Deep WM invasion', 'Ependymal (ventricular) Invasion'). overall_comment: The combination of advanced patient age and classic imaging features—a large, necrotic, midline-crossing, and deeply infiltrative mass with sharp FLAIR borders and absent T2-FLAIR mismatch—provides a textbook example of a glioblastoma. All three predictions (IDH-wildtype, 1p/19q non-codeleted, and WHO grade 4) are made with very high confidence and are internally consistent, leading to the integrated diagnosis of Glioblastoma, IDH-wildtype, CNS WHO grade 4.
